How the layers fit

The library stays understandable when each layer has one job. Personas describe who is operating, skills describe what they can do, tool-use recipes make a capability practical in a named tool, and playbooks coordinate the work.

A playbook is a reusable operating model for an outcome.

It defines stages, participants, handoffs, decision rights, shared state, quality gates, and learning loops. It does not replace the personas, skills, or tool-use recipes it calls.

  • Portable skills and quality signals
  • Resources, tools, and artifacts

Tool-use recipes

  • Required capability and prerequisites

  • Output, fallback, and verification

The way work is organized and handed off.

  • Decision points and quality gates

A Playbook is a reusable operating model for an outcome.

It defines stages, participants, handoffs, decision rights, shared state, quality gates, and learning loops. It references Personas, Skills, Operating Packs, and Tool-use recipes without copying their definitions.

Operating Pack references

A Playbook may require persistent domain context at one or more stages. Reference the Operating Pack by stable identity and scope instead of copying its rules into the outcome model.

Skill formation playbook

Create and integrate a reusable skill by combining bounded perspectives from the personas who perform the work, then formalize the result without losing its context.

Create and integrate a reusable skill

This playbook turns a multi-persona question into a reusable capability. It uses personas for perspective, Create-skill for formalization, and reconciliation to keep the rest of the system aligned.

Working model
01 / FRAMEScope the capabilityDefine the outcome, boundary, and reason this deserves a skill.
02 / SELECTChoose the lensesInvite only the personas whose work reveals a distinct part of the capability.
03 / SYNTHESIZECompare the perspectivesFind shared triggers, actions, tools, decisions, and quality signals.
04 / FORMALIZEUse Create-skillTurn the shared core into a structured skill with explicit boundaries.
05 / VALIDATETest quality and reuseCheck that the skill is recognizable, non-duplicative, and useful in a new context.
06 / RECONCILEIntegrate the systemUpdate affected personas, workflows, docs, relationships, and revision history.

Shared state keeps the playbook coherent

The orchestrator coordinates work through shared objects, not through vague handoffs. Each stage should read from and leave behind a traceable state.

Source-grounded context brief

Reader, goal, target, constraints, original source versions, proposed positioning, and unresolved questions. Use the application brief.

Evidence bank

Source experiences, outcomes, artifacts, decisions, metrics, confidence, and gaps.

Artifact versions and reviews

Each review names a version, criterion, passage/page, finding, action, and verdict. Reopen affected checks after edits. Review contract.

Decision + learning log

What changed, why it changed, what remains uncertain, and what would change the plan again.

What belongs in a playbook skill?

Yes, eventually. A dedicated playbooks skill should define outcomes, decompose stages, route work to existing personas and skills, manage shared state, enforce quality gates, preserve decision rights, and close the learning loop. It should call persona-research and persona-skills when new lenses or capabilities are needed instead of recreating their methods.

Change control

A playbook is not complete when one stage finishes; it is complete when the shared state and downstream artifacts are coherent.

Every playbook update ends with a conditional reconciliation gate.

When a stage changes a source, record, artifact, handoff, or quality gate, invoke $change-impact-reconciliation before handing the playbook back. Re-check participants, prerequisites, shared state, dependent artifacts, and the next stage. Read-only consultation stages skip the gate; prototype stages check isolation only.
